**Allowed origins** are set in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. The `cors({ origin: (origin) => … })` callback echoes the origin back only if it is one of these:

- exactly `http://localhost:4200`
- any origin ending in `.pages.dev`
- any origin ending in `.workers.dev`

Requests with no `Origin` header, and every other origin, get `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. The same middleware allows methods `GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS` and headers `Content-Type, Authorization`, with `maxAge: 86400`.

**Adding a custom domain:** add another condition inside the `origin` function, at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. For example, add `|| origin === 'https://play.example.com'` to the `if (...)`. Use an exact match for a single domain. For all subdomains, use `origin.endsWith('.example.com')`. That suffix check also matches lookalikes such as `evil-example.com`, so prefer `.endsWith('.example.com')` with the leading dot, or an exact match.

Don't put the domain in an array form of `origin`. Hono matches array entries as exact strings, so wildcards wouldn't work there (noted in `index.ts:20` and in `docs/code/worker/src/index.md`).

If the custom domain is also the frontend's host, check that the frontend's API base URL points at the Worker. I haven't looked at that. `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 covers CORS in more detail, and I didn't read it.
